tables.name: appointment
tables.what: One row per appointment version (a cancel or reschedule keeps the old row and adds a new one).
tables.purpose: The booking. Drives the pre-visit eligibility and authorization work, and the no-show and lead-time numbers. Not needed for revenue metrics, so Important, not Mandatory.
tables.metrics: No-show rate, cancellation rate, lead time, eligibility-verified-before-visit rate, appointment-to-claim days
tables.fallback: 1 scheduler API / HL7 / FHIR, 2 PM export, 3 rebuild from encounters (loses booking date, cancels, no-shows, pre-visit work)

cols.name: appointment_id
cols.desc: Stable ID of the record: the same on every version. The primary key is (appointment_id, version). Every link from another table uses appointment_id alone and takes the row with is_current = 1; an as-of view takes the highest version with modified_at (or loaded_at) on or before the date.
cols.fb: Generated by us on the first version
cols.why: Now the stable record ID; primary key is (appointment_id, version). Children no longer point at one version and get orphaned when the header changes.

cols.name: tenant_id
cols.desc: The client organisation the row belongs to.

cols.name: appointment_number
cols.desc: The client's own appointment ID. Restricted: used only to match the source system.
cols.fb: Hash of patient, provider, date, time

cols.name: practice_id
cols.desc: Billing entity.

cols.name: patient_id
cols.desc: The patient.

cols.name: appointment_date
cols.desc: Visit date; sets the 3-day and 1-day check timing.

cols.name: appointment_status
cols.desc: Booked, confirmed, arrived, completed, cancelled, no_show, rescheduled.
cols.fb: Derived: an encounter exists means completed; date passed with none means no_show (assumed)

cols.name: provider_id
cols.desc: Scheduled provider; utilization and no-shows by provider.

cols.name: payer_id
cols.desc: Insurer on file at booking. Not borrowed from the claim: no claim exists yet, and none ever will for a no-show.
cols.fb: Payer on the patient's last claim (marked assumed)

cols.name: coverage_id
cols.desc: The policy the eligibility check will test.
cols.why: Key width aligned with the parent table key.

cols.name: facility_id
cols.desc: Site capacity.

cols.name: start_time
cols.desc: Day utilization and ordering.

cols.name: booked_date
cols.desc: Lead time; the pre-visit checks key off it.

cols.name: appointment_type
cols.desc: New, follow_up, procedure, preventive, telehealth, emergency.
cols.fb: New if no history, else follow_up

cols.name: booked_via
cols.desc: Phone, portal, walk-in, referral.

cols.name: referring_provider_id
cols.desc: HMO referrals.

cols.name: referral_id
cols.desc: The referral this visit was booked under, when there is one.
cols.why: Visits used on a referral can be counted from the visits themselves, not guessed from dates.

cols.name: version
cols.desc: 1 for the first row; higher for each change.

cols.name: is_current
cols.desc: 1 on the latest version. Counts use current rows only.

cols.name: previous_appointment_id
cols.desc: Stable ID of a different record this one replaced (a reschedule booked as a new appointment, a replacement claim). Blank for ordinary version changes, which keep the same ID.

cols.name: created_at

cols.name: modified_at

tables.name: appointment_status_log
tables.what: One status change of an appointment: from which status to which, when, by whom and why.
tables.purpose: The appointment lifecycle as events (booked, confirmed, arrived, checked in, roomed, seen, checked out, cancelled, no-show, rescheduled). Append-only. Lead time, late cancels, no-show patterns and check-in to check-out times are measured from status_changed_at.
tables.metrics: Confirmation rate, late-cancel and no-show rate, reschedule frequency, check-in to checkout cycle time, wait time, changes by channel or staff
tables.fallback: 1 HL7 SIU messages or FHIR Appointment history, 2 PM appointment audit / status history report, 3 rebuilt from appointment versions (time = modified_at; source = rebuilt_from_appointment)

cols.name: change_channel

cols.name: reason_code

cols.desc: The load that wrote the row.

cols.desc: When the row was loaded.

tables.name: eligibility_check
tables.what: One 270/271 exchange: the question asked of a payer about a patient's coverage for a service date, and the answer that came back.
tables.purpose: Keeps the history that coverage.last_verified_* cannot: every check, its answer and the reason when it failed. Append-only; coverage keeps only the latest status.
tables.metrics: Checks done before the visit, share active, AAA reject rate by reason, coverage problems found before the visit, age of the last check at the visit, other-payer-primary finds, estimated patient cost inputs
tables.fallback: 1 Clearinghouse 270/271 log, 2 payer portal check keyed in, 3 coverage.last_verified_* only (one latest check, history lost)

cols.name: eligibility_check_id
cols.desc: Internal identity ID. Every join and link between tables uses this, so the client's number never has to be shown or masked in analytics.

cols.name: tenant_id
cols.desc: The client organisation the row belongs to.

cols.name: trace_number
cols.desc: Reference that ties the 270 to its 271 (TRN02). Unique per request: TRG + appointment id + check_sequence (+ -2 on the secondary payer).
cols.why: TRG + appointment id repeated on every re-check of the same appointment.

cols.name: check_sequence
cols.desc: Order of checks for the same appointment and coverage (1, 2, 3 ...). Makes trace_number unique.
cols.why: Repeat checks on one appointment produced the same trace number.

cols.name: appointment_id
cols.desc: Visit the check was done for.
cols.fb: Match on patient and service date

cols.name: coverage_id
cols.desc: Coverage that was checked.

cols.name: patient_id
cols.desc: Copied from the coverage so patient history needs no join.

cols.name: payer_id
cols.desc: Payer asked.

cols.name: practice_id
cols.desc: Reports by practice.

cols.name: is_secondary
cols.desc: 1 when the check was for the secondary coverage.

cols.name: check_date
cols.desc: Day the 271 was obtained; age of the check is service date minus this.

cols.name: check_ts
cols.desc: Exact time of the answer, to tell same-day repeats apart.

cols.name: service_date
cols.desc: Date of service asked about (DTP 291).

cols.name: service_type_code
cols.desc: Service type asked about (EQ01).

cols.name: is_active
cols.desc: 1 when the payer says coverage is active (EB 1), 0 when not active (EB 6). Blank when the payer rejected the request; CHECK: is_active is set or is_aaa_reject = 1.
cols.why: Blank on AAA rejects, so it cannot be Mandatory.

cols.name: is_aaa_reject
cols.desc: 1 when the payer answered with an AAA error, for example member not found.

cols.name: aaa_reason_code
cols.desc: AAA reason code (43, 72, 75 ...). Tells a typing error from no coverage.

cols.name: plan_begin_date

cols.desc: Coinsurance in the answer (EB A), as a fraction 0 to 1 (0.2000 = 20%).

cols.desc: Benefit level of the amounts (EB02): individual, family, employee_spouse.
cols.why: Deductible and out-of-pocket amounts mean different things per level.

cols.why: Estimates differ in and out of network.

tables.name: document
tables.what: One row per clinical or administrative document in the EMR (visit note, consent, advance notice, plan of care, result, letter, document pack): who, when, status, signatures. Never the content.
tables.purpose: The metadata layer for documentation work. It lets agents chase unsigned notes, check what a note documents, prove a consent or order is on file, and track which documents go with an authorization request or claim. Versioned: each change in status or signature is a new row, so signature lag and late entries can be measured as they were known.
tables.metrics: Unsigned-note count and age, signature lag, late-entry rate, addendum rate, co-signature backlog, documentation completeness by service group, consent on-file rate, share of authorization requests with a complete document pack
tables.fallback: 1 EHR document and note index (metadata export or HL7 MDM), 2 EHR note-status report from the PM, 3 summary on the encounter (note_status, note_signed_date, elements_documented) with one rebuilt row per encounter, 4 none (Note Chaser then reads only the encounter columns)

cols.fb: Generated by us on the first version

tables.name: claim_attachment
tables.what: One row per payer records request or attachment announcement for one claim: what was asked, when it is due, what we sent, and the payer's answer.
tables.purpose: Runs the payer-records workflow (pre-payment review, post-payment audit, attachment requests) and the attachment announcement on the claim. A request that covers several claims is several rows sharing the payer's reference number. Versioned: each status change (collecting, sent, acknowledged) is a new row.
tables.metrics: Open requests and days to due date, response lag, requests sent late, requests by payer and type, payer acknowledgement outcomes, claims denied for no attachment
tables.fallback: 1 EHR or portal request log, 2 claim 277 status request and PWK segment on the 837, 3 manual entry from the request letter

cols.name: claim_attachment_id

Every link from another table uses claim_attachment_id alone and takes the row with is_current = 1; an as-of view takes the highest version with modified_at (or loaded_at) on or before the date.
cols.fb: Generated by us on the first version
cols.why: Now the stable record ID; primary key is (claim_attachment_id, version). Children no longer point at one version and get orphaned when the header changes.

tables.name: agent_forecast
tables.what: One row per stored prediction: a cash, recoverable or claim payment forecast, with its range and, later, what actually happened.
tables.purpose: Agent output: written by the agent as it runs, never rebuilt from the canonical tables. Agents never write into the canonical tables; an approved change returns through the normal load as a new version row. Predictions are kept as made so accuracy is scored against what was said then. Filling in the actual is a new version; the earlier row stays.
tables.metrics: Forecast versus actual cash, WAPE, share of actuals inside the 80% range, claim payment chance calibration, recoverable forecast versus recovered, forecast by payer and week
tables.fallback: 1 written by the forecasting agent at run time, actual filled from 835 payments in ledger_entry, 2 forecast rebuilt from claim history (range lost, flagged by source = rebuilt_from_claims), 3 none: no backtest possible

cols.name: agent_forecast_id
cols.desc: Stable ID of the record: the same on every version. The primary key is (agent_forecast_id, version). Every link from another table uses agent_forecast_id alone and takes the row with is_current = 1; an as-of view takes the highest version with modified_at (or loaded_at) on or before the date.
cols.fb: Generated by us on the first version
cols.why: Now the stable record ID; primary key is (agent_forecast_id, version). Children no longer point at one version and get orphaned when the header changes.

tables.name: payer_rule
tables.what: One version of one rule: an authorization requirement, a bundling pair, a medical-necessity pair, a unit limit, a payer claim edit, a learned denial pattern or an agent detection rule, with the dates it applied.
tables.purpose: The rule library the prevention checks read. Rules change over time, so a change is a new version row with its own effective dates and a link to the row it replaced; a decision can always be traced to the exact version that ran. Source and learned evidence are codes and counts only, never free text.
tables.metrics: Rules in force by payer and family, learned rules waiting for approval, rules retired, rule hit and overturn rates (joined to agent_decision_check), rule age since last confirmed, share of synthetic placeholder rules
tables.fallback: 1 Payer policy or contract loaded with a source code, 2 CMS code-pair and unit-limit tables, 3 rule learned from our own denials (counts kept as evidence, needs approval), 4 practice-entered rule, 5 no rule row: the check is skipped and shown as skipped
